IR.rationale: Intermediate yields rising relative to policy while bill rates are not rising points to a higher term premium rather than expected tightening. Such a premium tends to be earned back, so subsequent excess bond returns are higher.

B.rationale: Stable high-grade spreads together with strong high-yield returns describe easy credit conditions. That supports the corporate and spread components of aggregate bond indices.

V.rationale: High oil uncertainty without safe-haven or monetary uncertainty signals growth and disinflation risk. That state tends to pull yields down.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities signal global risk appetite and capital flows that coincide with steady demand for duration and spread assets.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms is a quality, defensive tilt that tends to accompany falling yields.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar strength tightens US financial conditions and is disinflationary, which supports Treasury prices.

COM.rationale: Falling oil lowers inflation expectations and breakevens, which reduces nominal yields.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise flight-to-quality demand and the expected path of easier policy, both bullish for duration.

ENDG.rationale: Bond returns show mild reversal at weekly-to-quarterly horizons as term-premium shocks partially unwind.

IR.rationale: A sharp steepening alongside rising intermediate yields signals active repricing of the rate path and term premium. Such repricing episodes cluster in volatility.

B.rationale: Weak high-yield and EM sovereign returns mark broad risk-off. That raises the volatility of safe-haven and spread bonds alike.

V.rationale: Joint elevation of gold and equity implied volatility reflects cross-asset macro and monetary uncertainty that spills into rates volatility.

AP.rationale: Global equity weakness triggers flight-to-quality flows. Those flows raise realised variance in bond prices.

ST.rationale: Poor short-term reversal returns indicate strained liquidity provision, a sign of fragile market-making that raises volatility.

FX.rationale: A rapidly strengthening dollar reflects global dollar funding pressure, which is associated with higher volatility across fixed income.

COM.rationale: Commodity sell-offs signal global growth scares, which tend to bring large moves in yields.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions with falling breakevens describe a deflationary scare. Large yield moves then follow.

ENDG.rationale: Variance mean-reverts, so when recent variance is high, future variance tends to fall short of what persistence alone implies.

IR.rationale: Bear steepening, with long and intermediate yields rising versus policy, marks a term-premium sell-off. Such sell-offs show momentum and produce large duration losses.

B.rationale: Weak EM dollar bonds often reflect rising US yields and capital outflows, a state that precedes further bond losses.

V.rationale: High gold volatility captures uncertainty about real rates and monetary policy, which raises the left tail of bond returns.

AP.rationale: Value outperformance accompanies reflation and rising yields, which is a bearish state for duration.

ST.rationale: Junk and low-momentum rallies mark a reflationary risk-on rotation away from defensive assets. That rotation is associated with bond sell-offs.

FX.rationale: Dollar weakness, especially against the euro, signals global reflation and reduced foreign demand for Treasuries. Both raise the risk of large losses.

COM.rationale: Rising oil lifts inflation expectations and nominal yields, which fattens the loss tail.

MC.rationale: Financial stress combined with rising breakevens points to rate-driven stress, a tantrum-like state in which bonds are the source of risk rather than the hedge.

ENDG.rationale: Bond sell-offs show short-horizon persistence, so recent weak returns raise the chance of a further large loss.

IR.rationale: An elevated term premium without front-end tightening tends to unwind. That unwinding can produce outsized rallies.

B.rationale: Compressing high-grade spreads with strong high-yield returns indicate supportive credit conditions that lift aggregate bond returns.

V.rationale: Elevated oil and equity uncertainty set up flight-to-quality episodes that produce large Treasury rallies.

AP.rationale: Strong equity markets coincide with abundant liquidity and risk-bearing capacity, which supports outsized gains in duration and spread bonds.

ST.rationale: Healthy reversal returns indicate well-functioning liquidity provision, which allows sharp price rallies.

FX.rationale: Strong carry currencies signal global search for yield and inflows into dollar fixed income.

COM.rationale: Rising silver reflects falling real rates and a weaker policy outlook, both associated with strong bond rallies.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise the odds of policy easing and flight-to-quality, which fattens the upper tail of bond returns.

ENDG.rationale: After weak recent returns, term-premium reversal raises the chance of a large rebound.
